newsitem.title: YUGOSLAVIA: SOCCER-YUGOSLAVIA OPTIMISTIC AHEAD OF QUALIFIER WITH CZECHS.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-YUGOSLAVIA OPTIMISTIC AHEAD OF QUALIFIER WITH CZECHS.

text.p: Yugoslavia were optimistic of maintaining their winning record on Friday ahead of their group six World Cup qualifier against European championship finalists the Czech Republic at the Red Star stadium on Sunday.
"We are going to give it all we've got and I believe there will be no problem," midfielder Slavisa Jokanovic told the Belgrade newspaper Blic.
But Yugoslavia suffered a setback this week when AC Milan midfielder Dejan Savicevic was ruled out through injury.

Yugoslavia head the group with three wins from as many matches, scoring 17 goals along the way while conceding just two, although their victories came against the group's weaker teams -- Malta and the Faroe Islands.

The Czech Republic, who lost in extra-time to Germany in this year's Euro 96 final, opened their World Cup campaign with a 6-0 victory over Malta and played out a scoreless draw with Spain in their last encounter.
In 31 matches between the national teams of former Yugoslavia and Czechoslovakia, the Czechs have won 18 times.
"I am not afraid of anything or anyone," Yugoslav manager Slobodan Santrac said.
"Over the past days we have worked on adjusting our game and been viewing tapes of the Czechs play.
"Our team is exceptionally strong, as individuals and as a collective. So the Czechs have something to worry about."
